edu-dopamine-01.title: Wanting is not the same as liking
edu-dopamine-01.summary: A short check after the dopamine sheet: what the messenger is actually tied to.
edu-dopamine-01.goal: Distinguish dopamine’s role in wanting and learning from the idea that it is “the pleasure molecule”.
edu-dopamine-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, dopamine is most closely tied to which of these?
edu-dopamine-01.explain: The sheet links dopamine more to wanting, learning from prediction error, and deciding what is worth trying than to pleasure itself. Liking depends on several systems. A sudden rise is not the same as being happier.

options.wanting: Wanting, learning, and deciding what is worth trying
options.pleasure: Pleasure itself — it is “the pleasure molecule”
options.meter: A personal meter of days without use

edu-serotonin-01.title: Not a happiness tank
edu-serotonin-01.summary: A check after the serotonin sheet: what 5-HT does and does not measure.
edu-serotonin-01.goal: See why calling serotonin “the happiness molecule” compresses too much, including the split between blood and brain.
edu-serotonin-01.prompt: Why is it misleading to treat serotonin as “the happiness molecule”?
edu-serotonin-01.explain: 5-HT modulates many systems at once. A sudden rise is not more happiness. Most of the body’s serotonin is not in the brain, and the molecule does not freely cross the blood–brain barrier, so a change in blood serotonin is not a reading of brain serotonin.

options.many_systems: It modulates many systems; a rise is not more happiness, and blood serotonin is not brain serotonin
options.blood_equals_brain: A blood test is a direct reading of brain serotonin and mood
options.happiness_tank: Serotonin exists only in the brain, where it fills a happiness tank

edu-gaba-01.title: Inhibition is not switching the brain off
edu-gaba-01.summary: A check after the GABA sheet: what “inhibitory” means in a network.
edu-gaba-01.goal: Understand GABA as a way some neurons fire less or with a different rhythm — not as a universal off switch or as alcohol itself.
edu-gaba-01.prompt: What does it mean that GABA is the main inhibitory messenger in the adult brain?
edu-gaba-01.explain: To inhibit is to make some neurons less likely to fire, or to fire with a different rhythm. It is not “switching the brain off.” Alcohol is not GABA: among other actions, it can potentiate some GABA-A receptors so they answer more strongly to GABA already there.

options.network_brake: It makes some neurons less likely to fire, or changes their rhythm — it does not switch the brain off
options.brain_off: It switches the whole brain off, which is the same as sleep
options.alcohol_is_gaba: Alcohol is GABA, so a drink replaces the messenger

edu-receptors-01.title: Occupying a receptor is not the same as activating it
edu-receptors-01.summary: A check after the receptors sheet: agonists, antagonists, and cocaine’s contrast.
edu-receptors-01.goal: Separate activation from occupancy, and receptor action from blocking a transporter.
edu-receptors-01.prompt: On the educational sheet, how do an agonist and an antagonist differ?
edu-receptors-01.explain: An agonist activates the receptor, or a substantial fraction of its activity. An antagonist occupies the site without mimicking that activation. Cocaine’s best-known dopaminergic move is not opening a dopamine receptor: it blocks DAT, so dopamine already released is cleared more slowly.

options.occupancy: An agonist activates (or a large fraction of that activity); an antagonist occupies without mimicking that activation
options.same_name: They are two names for the same ligand at the same door
options.cocaine_is_key: Cocaine is a key that opens D1 and D2 receptors the way nicotine opens nicotinic ones

edu-tolerance-01.title: Tolerance is not addiction
edu-tolerance-01.summary: A check after the tolerance sheet: a change of sensitivity, not a diagnosis.
edu-tolerance-01.goal: Define pharmacological tolerance without equating it with addiction or with a tank running dry.
edu-tolerance-01.prompt: What does pharmacological tolerance mean in this educational sheet?
edu-tolerance-01.explain: Tolerance is a drop in the response to the same dose when exposure is repeated. It is not a moral judgement and not, by itself, addiction or a substance use disorder. It is not the brain simply running out of a messenger, and Soma cannot assign you a universal curve.

options.sensitivity: A drop in response to the same dose with repeated exposure — not the same as addiction
options.equals_addiction: Proof of addiction; one weaker coffee is enough to diagnose a disorder
options.empty_tank: The brain running out of the messenger, on a curve Soma can read in you

edu-neuroadaptation-01.title: Adaptation is not the same as damage
edu-neuroadaptation-01.summary: A check after the neuroadaptation sheet: plasticity versus loss of cells.
edu-neuroadaptation-01.goal: Distinguish functional change in circuits from neurodegeneration, and from a fixed recovery calendar.
edu-neuroadaptation-01.prompt: How does the sheet distinguish neuroadaptation from neurodegeneration?
edu-neuroadaptation-01.explain: Neuroadaptation is mainly a change of function — plasticity — and sometimes of synapse architecture. Neurodegeneration is loss or injury of nerve cells. They are not the same thing, and stopping use does not reset the nervous system on a universal calendar this app can apply.

options.plasticity: Neuroadaptation is mainly functional change; neurodegeneration is loss or injury of nerve cells
options.cell_death: Every adaptation to caffeine or nicotine is the same as losing neurons
options.fixed_calendar: They are the same process, and the brain returns to a snapshot on a fixed number of days

edu-dependence-01.title: Physical dependence is not addiction
edu-dependence-01.summary: A check after the dependence sheet: a borrowed equilibrium versus a clinical diagnosis.
edu-dependence-01.goal: Separate physical dependence and withdrawal from a substance use disorder.
edu-dependence-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, how does physical dependence differ from a substance use disorder?
edu-dependence-01.explain: Physical dependence is an adaptation of the body to the repeated presence of a substance. Withdrawal may appear when it is cut down, but withdrawal alone does not determine a diagnosis. A substance use disorder is assessed clinically with a broader set of criteria. You can also have a disorder with little classic withdrawal, depending on the substance.

options.not_disorder: It is a bodily adaptation; withdrawal by itself does not diagnose a substance use disorder
options.same_as_addiction: They are the same diagnosis: if stopping feels bad, that is already addiction
options.soma_meter: Without alcohol-like withdrawal (tremor, seizures), there is no physical dependence

edu-metabolism-01.title: Clearing the plasma does not reset the nervous system
edu-metabolism-01.summary: A check after the metabolism sheet: transforming a molecule is not the same as undoing adaptations.
edu-metabolism-01.goal: See why biotransformation is not neuronal recovery, and why half-life is not duration of effect.
edu-metabolism-01.prompt: What does the educational sheet say about the metabolism of a substance?
edu-metabolism-01.explain: Metabolism is the set of reactions that modify a molecule, often in the liver. Processing and eliminating it does not by itself undo nervous-system adaptations. Plasma half-life is not the same as duration of effect: active metabolites and the lag between concentration and response also matter.

options.half_life_is_effect: Plasma half-life is the same thing as how long the effect lasts
options.not_reset: Transforming and eliminating the molecule does not by itself undo nervous-system adaptations
options.soma_hours: Once the substance is gone from plasma, tolerance and nervous-system adaptations have gone too

edu-glutamate-01.title: Excitatory does not mean toxic
edu-glutamate-01.summary: A check after the glutamate sheet: what “excitatory” means in a network.
edu-glutamate-01.goal: Distinguish everyday excitatory transmission from excitotoxicity, which is a pathological path, not a drink.
edu-glutamate-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, what does it mean that glutamate is the main excitatory messenger?
edu-glutamate-01.explain: Excitatory means it favours transmission: it pushes a neighbouring neuron toward firing threshold. It does not mean “dangerous” or “toxic by nature.” Excitotoxicity is a pathological path studied in injury such as ischaemia; it is not the description of a cup of coffee or a single drink.

options.poison: It is an excitatory poison: its mere existence damages neurons
options.one_drink: A drink or a coffee is the same phenomenon as excitotoxicity
options.favours_transmission: It favours the neighbouring neuron approaching firing threshold — it is not dangerous by nature

edu-norepinephrine-01.title: Brain noradrenaline is not a blood test
edu-norepinephrine-01.summary: A check after the noradrenaline sheet: attention and wakefulness are not circulating catecholamines.
edu-norepinephrine-01.goal: Keep noradrenaline’s role in the brain apart from catecholamines in blood, and apart from dopamine.
edu-norepinephrine-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, what is noradrenaline mainly doing in the brain?
edu-norepinephrine-01.explain: In the brain it takes part in attention, wakefulness and helping some signals stand out. That is not the same as catecholamines circulating in blood or measured in urine, even if the name matches. Being built from dopamine does not make them the same signal, nor a permanent alarm.

options.not_blood_map: It takes part in attention and wakefulness, and helps some signals stand out — it is not only “getting nervous”
options.urine_is_focus: It is a continuous alarm: more noradrenaline in blood means more stress and more attention in the brain
options.same_as_dopamine: Noradrenaline and dopamine are the same signal because one is built from the other

edu-acetylcholine-01.title: Nicotine is not acetylcholine
edu-acetylcholine-01.summary: A check after the acetylcholine sheet: an exogenous alkaloid is not the endogenous messenger.
edu-acetylcholine-01.goal: Separate nicotine from acetylcholine, and nicotinic receptors from muscarinic ones.
edu-acetylcholine-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, how do nicotine and acetylcholine relate?
edu-acetylcholine-01.explain: Nicotine is not acetylcholine. It roughly mimics acetylcholine at some nicotinic receptors, not at muscarinic ones and not at every synapse. Stimulating a nicotinic receptor is not “raising brain acetylcholine” as if it were a store.

options.is_the_messenger: Nicotine is acetylcholine: it replaces the messenger throughout the body
options.mimic_some: Nicotine roughly mimics acetylcholine at some nicotinic receptors, not at muscarinic ones
options.raises_store: Opening a nicotinic receptor is “raising brain acetylcholine” like filling a tank

edu-adenosine-01.title: Caffeine does not empty a sleep tank
edu-adenosine-01.summary: A check after the adenosine sheet: occupying a receptor is not draining a liquid.
edu-adenosine-01.goal: See caffeine as an antagonist at adenosine receptors, not as emptying a sleep tank or as cocaine’s main move.
edu-adenosine-01.prompt: What is caffeine’s main move in this educational sheet?
edu-adenosine-01.explain: Caffeine is a competitive antagonist at adenosine receptors — mainly A1 and A2A at usual cup doses: it occupies the site and lifts part of the brake. It does not empty a tank of sleep, and it does not copy cocaine’s main move. Lifting that brake is not “raising dopamine” the way cocaine does.

options.empties_tank: It empties a store of adenosine, and with it sleep pressure disappears
options.blocks_dat: It copies cocaine’s main move: stopping already-released dopamine from being cleared
options.antagonist: It is a competitive antagonist at adenosine receptors (mainly A1 and A2A): it occupies the site and lifts part of the brake

edu-endorphin-01.title: Endorphins are not morphine
edu-endorphin-01.summary: A check after the endorphin sheet: endogenous peptides are not a pleasure tap.
edu-endorphin-01.goal: Distinguish endorphins from morphine, and from a single account of pleasure or of a runner’s high.
edu-endorphin-01.prompt: What does the educational sheet clarify about endorphins?
edu-endorphin-01.explain: Endorphins are opioid peptides the body makes itself. They are not morphine or heroin. Endorphin, enkephalin and dynorphin are not three names for pleasure: dynorphins, in many models, push more toward aversion. The so-called runner’s high has also been linked to endocannabinoids; a single molecule is not a universal explanation.

options.own_peptides: They are opioid peptides the body makes; they are not morphine, and not a single pleasure switch
options.are_morphine: Endorphin is the scientific name for the morphine the brain produces
options.runner_meter: The runner’s high is explained only by a surge of β-endorphin, the universal pleasure molecule

edu-endocannabinoid-01.title: THC is not the body’s own messenger
edu-endocannabinoid-01.summary: A check after the endocannabinoid sheet: a plant agonist is not anandamide or 2-AG.
edu-endocannabinoid-01.goal: Separate THC from endogenous ligands, and “the body’s cannabis” from retrograde signalling.
edu-endocannabinoid-01.prompt: According to the educational sheet, how do the endocannabinoid system and THC relate?
edu-endocannabinoid-01.explain: THC is not anandamide or 2-AG. It occupies CB1 receptors that already had their own ligands, with different kinetics. The system is not “the body’s cannabis,” and cannabis does not start by flooding the brain with anandamide.

options.body_cannabis: The system is “the body’s cannabis,” and THC exactly copies those ligands
options.not_the_ligands: THC is not anandamide or 2-AG: it occupies CB1 receptors that already had their own ligands
options.makes_anandamide: Cannabis first floods the brain with anandamide
